summary: Overnight intelligence-driven follow-up on eaAcceptanceRate UNAVAILABLE targets. The Wave 5 closure pass already covered the cluster systematically (199 UNAVAILABLE = 65% terminal). This pass: (1) verified 6 high-yield CDS-blank candidates (Stevens, SCU, U Miami, Clemson, VT, UMN, UDel, UVM) via WebSearch + direct CDS PDF fetch — all confirmed UNAVAILABLE (CDS C22 either has EA=Yes with counts blank, or aggregator estimates fail the 2-source bar). UDel CDS 2022-23 C22 directly confirms EA=Yes, counts blank. UVM CDS 2024-25 C22 directly confirms EA=Yes (Nov 1 / Late December), counts blank — only ED has counts (479 apps / 449 admits). (2) Wrote canonical PROGRAM_NOT_OFFERED notes for 23 targets where Wave 5 left notes empty — verified each school's EA status via official .edu sources. (3) Sharpened notes for a few schools where Wave 5 had a less-specific reason. Net effect: 0 new CLOSED (research confirmed schools genuinely do not publish), but 23 UNAVAILABLE entries gain proper structural reasons so future re-runs treat them as truly terminal. Recommend: leave all eaAcceptanceRate values as currently set; apply only the 23+ note upgrades below.

noNewClosures: 0 new CLOSED targets in this overnight pass. Rationale: every promising aggregator-reported EA admit rate (Stevens 72.7%, UVM 72.6%, UDel 70.0%, Clemson 50-55%, U Miami) fails the 2-independent-source verification bar when checked against the school's official CDS or admissions reporting. The data is genuinely suppressed: schools that offer EA but don't publish counts have made a deliberate institutional choice not to disclose. Fabricating a value would violate ADR-0020 and the no-fabrication rule. EA closure ceiling remains structurally bounded: the field will plateau at ~65-70% terminal until enough schools either (a) start publishing EA admit data in CDS C22, or (b) we accept aggregator-tier DERIVED data with appropriate confidence floor (engineering change, not a closure-pass change).
